title: Grateful Dead Live at The Spectrum on 1985-04-08
lineage: MC > Playback on Marantz PRD505 (azimuth adjusted) > Marantz Intergrated Stereo Amp MP-68 > SBLive! > Sound Forge normalization > WAV > CDWave > WAVs > mkwAC > SHNs
source: unknown shotgun mics > Sony D6 > Maxell MX 90s (MC)

ai_review.summary: A clean audience tape captures the Spectrum’s vibe, but the performance is uneven – Revolution shines while the rest of the show feels rushed and lackluster.
ai_review.review: The AUD recording is praised for its vivid, immersive sound that puts listeners right in the Spectrum, making it a strong technical document. Musically the concert is a mixed bag: early moments are exciting with a standout “Revolution” (called a masterpiece by some), but the band drifts into sloppiness and fatigue later on, leading reviewers to describe the overall show as weak and ragged.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is judged average‑to‑below average (≈2.5/5) while recording quality is good (≈4/5); weighted combination yields about a 3‑star rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, immersive capture of the Spectrum atmosphere; praised as “great sound” with no major flaws noted.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early excitement gives way to a rushed, ragged spring ’85 feel; momentum drops after the first set and the second half feels sluggish.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia described as gasping for air and weaker later in the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh receives affectionate shout‑outs (“Tish & Phil: I love ya!!”).
